_meta.description: Document-rules config for partition_deed — Partition deed of Hindu Joint Family / Mitakshara coparcenary. Post-HSA 2005 amendment, daughters are coparceners by birth. Cites Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1 — daughters get coparcenary rights even if father died before 2005 amendment. Registration mandatory if value > Rs.100 (Registration Act S.17).
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Vineeta Sharma is non-negotiable — daughters' coparcenary rights post-2005 must be reflected. Stamp duty often higher than sale deed where shares reduced.

title: Partition Deed (Hindu Joint Family — Mitakshara Coparcenary)

DEED OF PARTITION

This Deed of Partition is executed on this {date} at {place}.

BETWEEN the parties listed in the Schedule of Parties below, being all the coparceners / members of the Hindu Joint Family of late {common_ancestor}, with members styling themselves jointly as parties of all parts.

promptInstructions: Draft a PARTITION DEED of Hindu Joint Family / Mitakshara coparcenary property.

BACKGROUND — Hindu joint family is governed by Mitakshara (most of India incl. Bihar, Jharkhand, UP, Delhi) OR Dayabhaga (West Bengal, Assam). In Mitakshara: coparcenary is a body of male and female members who acquire interest in joint family property by birth. Coparcenary extends to 4 degrees from a common ancestor.

CRITICAL — Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, w.e.f. 9 September 2005, amended S.6 of HSA 1956 to provide that DAUGHTERS OF A COPARCENER SHALL BY BIRTH BECOME COPARCENERS in their own right in the same manner as sons. Daughters have same rights and liabilities as sons.

CRITICAL CASE — Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1, three-judge bench, OVERRULED Prakash v. Phulavati (2016) 2 SCC 36 to the extent inconsistent: Daughters' coparcenary rights are RETROSPECTIVE — daughters get coparcenary rights from BIRTH, regardless of whether father was alive on 9 September 2005. Earlier decisions requiring father to be alive on 2005 commencement date are OVERRULED.

S.6 HSA (amended): Notional partition concept — for purposes of devolution under proviso, a deemed partition is presumed to have taken place immediately before death of coparcener; coparcener's share devolves by intestate / testate succession under HSA.

Cite supporting cases: 
   - Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1 — daughters' retrospective coparcenary rights.
   - Danamma @ Suman Surpur v. Amar (2018) 3 SCC 343.
   - Arunachala Gounder v. Ponnusamy (2022) — clarified self-acquired property devolution for sole daughter Hindu females.

MUST IDENTIFY: who are the coparceners? Apply the test:
   - All living male and female lineal descendants of common ancestor within 4 degrees.
   - Post 2005 — daughters AND daughters' children (descendants of daughters who are coparceners) are coparceners by birth.
   - Widows of pre-deceased coparceners — get share by notional partition (Class I heir for husband's notional share).
   - Adopted children — same rights as natural-born after valid Hindu adoption.
EXCLUDE FROM COPARCENARY: married daughters' husbands (not coparceners); mothers (Class I heirs but not coparceners themselves); sister of common ancestor (collateral, not in line).

MINOR COPARCENER: Minor's share is interest in coparcenary. Partition affecting minor's interest requires court permission under Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 OR Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. Without court order, partition is voidable at instance of minor on attaining majority. FLAG prominently.
STRUCTURE OF PARTITION DEED:
Para 1: Title 'DEED OF PARTITION'.
Para 2: Recital of joint family — genealogy from common ancestor; school of Hindu law (Mitakshara).
Para 3: Schedule of parties — all coparceners + adult members with full identification.

Para 4: Daughters' coparcenary recital — affirm that all daughters (and daughters of daughters, granddaughters in line) are coparceners by birth per HSA S.6 (as amended 2005) and Vineeta Sharma (2020).

Para 5: Recital of joint property — set out properties (immovable in Schedule I; movable in Schedule II; business in Schedule III; liabilities in Schedule IV); state how property was acquired (ancestral / blended / accretions).

Para 6: Recital that parties wish to effect partition because [reason — family settlement, separation of branches, professional separation, etc.]. State that all members consent freely without coercion.

Para 7: METHOD OF PARTITION:
   (a) By metes and bounds — specific properties allotted to each sharer in lieu of share.
   (b) By specified shares — sharing percentage, then properties physically divided per share.
   (c) With owelty — where physical division not equal, balancing cash payment to make shares equal.
Para 8: ALLOTMENT — separately set out: 'Schedule A — Allotment to [Sharer 1]'; 'Schedule B — Allotment to [Sharer 2]'; etc. Each schedule lists immovable + movable + cash allotted to that sharer.
Para 9: OWELTY clause (if applicable) — specify cash payments between sharers.

Para 10: MUTUAL RELEASE — 'Each of the sharers hereby releases, relinquishes and gives up all rights, title and interest in the properties allotted to the other sharers under the respective Schedules, and shall have no claim whatsoever against the others'.

Para 11: COVENANT FOR QUIET ENJOYMENT — 'Each sharer shall be entitled to peacefully and quietly hold, enjoy and dispose of the properties allotted under his/her Schedule absolutely as separate property'.
Para 12: APPORTIONMENT OF LIABILITIES — joint debts apportioned (typically equally OR pro rata to share value).
Para 13: MUTATION CLAUSE — each sharer authorised to apply for mutation in revenue and municipal records.

Para 14: STAMP DUTY — partition deed stamp duty varies state-to-state. Often:
   - Bihar: ~3% of value of separated share + 2% registration.
   - Jharkhand: similar — % of value of separated share.
   - UP: 2% on partition deed value + 1% registration.
   - Delhi: 2% on value of separated share + 1% registration.
   IMPORTANT — where partition reduces one sharer's share below his/her actual coparcenary entitlement, the difference may be treated as GIFT or SALE — higher stamp duty + capital gains implications. FLAG.

Para 15: COURT PERMISSION FOR MINOR — recite that natural guardian executes for minor, AND that court order under HMG Act / GWA has been obtained (cite order number, date, court). If not obtained — flag risk that minor may avoid partition on majority.
Para 16: INDEMNITY — mutual indemnity for breach.
Para 17: GOVERNING LAW — Hindu Succession Act, 1956 as amended.
Schedules I-IV (property) + Schedules A, B, C... (allotments) appended.
Two witnesses' attestation.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

Note on FAMILY ARRANGEMENT vs PARTITION DEED: A FAMILY ARRANGEMENT is a wider concept including settlement of disputes; courts treat genuine family arrangements indulgently per Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation (1976) 3 SCC 119. Where dispute being settled in addition to partition — consider family settlement deed (may have lower stamp duty in some states).

Note on ORAL PARTITION + MEMORANDUM: Oral partition followed by a memorandum of partition (recording what already happened) may avoid registration / lower stamp duty — but courts scrutinise such memoranda; risk of being held a partition deed in substance. Cite Roshan Singh v. Zile Singh (1988) Supp SCC 718.

Note on INCOME TAX — partition of HUF: complete partition extinguishes HUF (or partial — partial recognised pre-1980, post-1980 partial partitions of registered HUF not recognised by IT Dept under S.171 ITA). Where HUF is taxable entity — Form for recording partition with Income Tax Officer mandatory.

sections.description: Coparcenary; daughters' rights (post 2005 amendment); notional partition
General rules of succession in case of males
General rules of succession in case of Hindu females
Earlier disability of females in dwelling house — repealed
Power of natural guardian — court permission for alienation / partition involving minor
Court permission for transfer of minor's property
Compulsory registration of partition deed where immovable property value > Rs.100
Partition stamp duty — state-specific; based on value of separated share
Recording of partition of HUF — only complete partitions recognised post-1980
Decree in partition suits — preliminary + final

filing_checklist: Stamp paper of correct denomination per state Article 45 — based on value of separated share
Joint family genealogical tree / pedigree certificate
Original title documents of all joint property
Encumbrance Certificate (EC) — past 13 years for each property
Mutation entries / Jamabandi / Khatauni / Khatian extracts — current for each property
Property tax receipts up to date
All adult coparceners' ID — PAN + Aadhaar
Where minor coparcener — natural guardian's ID + COURT ORDER permitting partition under HMG Act / GWA
Birth certificates of all coparceners (to establish relationship and capacity)
Where widow's share included — death certificate of pre-deceased coparcener
Marriage certificate(s) of daughters (where included as coparceners — to establish identity post-marriage)
All adult coparceners (and natural guardians of minors) physically present at Sub-Registrar
Photographs of all parties (2 each)
Two adult witnesses with own ID proofs
Where HUF income tax assessment exists — Form under S.171 ITA to be filed with Assessing Officer recording complete partition; AO order under S.171 needed for IT Dept to discontinue HUF status
Registration at Sub-Registrar within 4 months of execution (S.23 Registration Act)
Post-registration: mutation applications in each sharer's name in revenue / municipal records
Update bank accounts / FDs / demat / shares as per allotment
Where partition under-allots a coparcener — flag potential gift tax / capital gains consequence
Lawie disclaimer included

daughters_included must be specified — if 'no_being_excluded_for_specific_reason_flag', insert prominent disclaimer about Vineeta Sharma compliance risk
